column2: The full code is about 6,000 lines (the web panel inside it is compressed): download robot_otak.ino. Do not upload a file that already contains your token and API keys anywhere public.

six tiles: Musik (SD songs, radio, podcasts, Quran recitation), Info (robot status, weather, prayer times, news, calendar, exchange rates, Wikipedia), Alat (motion modes, camera, alarm, timer, calculator, flashlight, translator, notes, voice recorder, photo gallery), Main (rock-paper-scissors, tic-tac-toe, 2048, tap-to-fly), Pesan (messages), and Setelan (settings). Buttons act when your finger lifts; the ◀ button at top left goes back. Long lists (114 surahs, hundreds of songs) have << and >> buttons to jump 5 pages
Screen: Musik → Podcast

the podcast list from DAFTAR_PODCAST in the code (the default is SBS Indonesian, with a new episode every day). Tap a podcast to see its 15 newest episodes, and tap an episode to play it; there are JEDA (pause), STOP, and volume buttons. To add a podcast, find its page on podnews.net and copy its RSS address into DAFTAR_PODCAST. Podcasts exclusive to Spotify or Noice have no open RSS, so they cannot be played
Screen: Musik → Murottal (Quran recitation), or Telegram /murottal 36

all 114 surahs. Tap a surah to play it; when it finishes, the next surah plays by itself. The Qari button picks the reciter (Alafasy, Abdul Basit, Al-Ghamdi, As-Sudais, Al-Husary, Al-Muaiqly, Ad-Dosari) from mp3quran.net. To play without internet, put files on the SD card in a /murottal folder with three-digit names: 001.mp3 to 114.mp3; files on the SD card always play first
Screen: Main → Tic-tac-toe

you are X, Zond is O, and the first move alternates. Mudah (easy) level: half of Zond's moves are random. Sulit (hard) level: Zond calculates every possibility, so the best you can do is a draw. The score counts until you change level
Screen: Main → 2048
swipe the board left, right, up, or down (or use the arrow buttons); two tiles with the same number merge. The best score is kept when the robot is switched off
Screen: Main → Ketuk terbang (tap to fly)
tap the screen to make the bird rise and fly through the gaps between the pipes. The best score is kept
Screen: Setelan → WiFi

the WiFi networks around the robot. Tap one, type its password with the on-screen keyboard, then SAMBUNG (connect). This WiFi is saved and tried first when the robot starts; if it fails, the robot uses WIFI_NAMA from the code. PAKAI WIFI KODE (use the code's WiFi) forgets that choice. If the robot started without WiFi, it restarts itself after connecting so the web panel and Telegram start too
On-screen keyboard (the KETIK button in Catatan, Penerjemah, Wikipedia, and the WiFi password)
lowercase letters; ^ for one capital letter, 123 and #+= for numbers and symbols, hold <- to delete quickly. The keys are small: press right in the middle of the letter

The podcast says "gagal diambil" (failed to load) or an episode makes no sound: the RSS address has moved or the episode is not MP3/AAC. Try opening the RSS address in a browser, and check the [audio] lines in the Serial Monitor.

Quran recitation makes no sound although WiFi is connected: the reciter address on mp3quran.net may have changed. Compare DAFTAR_QARI with the server field at https://mp3quran.net/api/v3/reciters, or use files on the SD card.
Tap-to-fly feels choppy: this 2.8" screen manages about 20 frames per second over the SPI wires. Raise LAYAR_MHZ to 40 if the wires are short; if the screen becomes striped, set it back to 27.
Your home WiFi is not in the list: the ESP32 only supports 2.4 GHz WiFi, and hidden networks are not shown. Turn on 2.4 GHz on the router, or put the name in WIFI_NAMA.
